title: Neurotensin analog PD149163 attenuates endotoxemia-induced brain dysfunction and behavioural deficits via modulating CRP, GABAergic and NRF2 signalling pathways in mice: In vivo, in silico and network pharmacology analyses.
one_liner_zh: 该文研究神经降压素类似物PD149163在小鼠内毒素血症脑功能障碍中的神经保护作用，涉及体内实验和网络药理学，但无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Endotoxemia-induced brain dysfunction is a complex neurological condition, with growing evidence underscoring the critical roles of neuroinflammation and oxidative stress in its pathogenesis. In this context, the current study was undertaken to evaluate the neuroprotective efficacy of the neuropeptide neurotensin analog PD149163 against endotoxemia-induced brain dysfunction and behavioural impairments in mice. Swiss-albino mice (female/08-weeks/25 +/- 2.5 g) were divided into 6 groups: Group-I/control; Groups II and III were treated with 50 mug/kg BW and 100 mug/kg BW of PD149163, respectively, for 4 weeks. Groups IV-VI were injected with LPS (1 mg/kg BW; 5 days), followed by PD149163 exposure to Group-V/LPS + PD(L) (50 mug/kg BW) and Group-VI/LPS + PD(H) (100 mug/kg BW) for 4 weeks. Both the LPS and PD149163 were given intraperitoneally. LPS elevated circulatory proinflammatory (TNF-alpha/IL6), proapoptotic/CAS3 biomarkers and decreased anti-inflammatory/IL10, antiapoptotic/BCL2 proteins. Endotoxemia attenuated the brain oxidative defence via decreasing antioxidants (SOD/CAT) while increasing the pro-oxidants (LPO/LOOH). LPS-induced upregulated mCRP (plasma) and hsCRP (brain) cause blood-brain barrier disruption, leading to neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration, reflected in the histopathology of CA1/CA3/DG of the hippocampus and PVN of the hypothalamus. LPS-induced brain dysfunction impairs locomotor activity, induces anxiety and depression-like behaviours with cognitive impairment, while also diminishing neurotransmitter GABA release. Treatment with PD(H) for 4 weeks significantly improved the behavioural deficits and reversed biochemical and histopathological alterations. Our in silico/PPI analysis suggests PD149163 binds and inhibits KEAP1 (Kelch-like ECH-associated protein-1) and acts as Nrf2 (nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2) activator. In conclusion, the current study demonstrates the neuroprotective effects of PD149163, potentially through modulation of Nrf2 pathway.
abstract_zh: 内毒素血症诱导的脑功能障碍是一种复杂的神经系统疾病，越来越多的证据强调神经炎症和氧化应激在其发病机制中的关键作用。在此背景下，本研究旨在评估神经肽神经降压素类似物PD149163对小鼠内毒素血症诱导的脑功能障碍和行为损伤的神经保护功效。瑞士白化小鼠（雌性/8周龄/25 ± 2.5 g）分为6组：第I组/对照组；第II组和第III组分别用50 μg/kg体重和100 μg/kg体重的PD149163处理4周。第IV-VI组注射LPS（1 mg/kg体重；5天），随后第V组/LPS + PD(L)（50 μg/kg体重）和第VI组/LPS + PD(H)（100 μg/kg体重）暴露于PD149163，持续4周。LPS和PD149163均通过腹腔注射给药。LPS升高了循环促炎因子（TNF-α/IL6）、促凋亡/CAS3生物标志物，并降低了抗炎因子/IL10、抗凋亡/BCL2蛋白。内毒素血症通过降低抗氧化剂（SOD/CAT）同时增加促氧化剂（LPO/LOOH）削弱了脑氧化防御。LPS诱导的上调mCRP（血浆）和hsCRP（脑）导致血脑屏障破坏，引发神经炎症和神经退行性变，这反映在海马CA1/CA3/DG和下丘脑PVN的组织病理学中。LPS诱导的脑功能障碍损害运动活动，诱导焦虑和抑郁样行为并伴有认知障碍，同时减少神经递质GABA的释放。用PD(H)处理4周显著改善了行为缺陷，并逆转了生化和组织病理学改变。我们的计算机模拟/PPI分析表明，PD149163结合并抑制KEAP1（Kelch样ECH相关蛋白-1），并作为Nrf2（核因子E2相关因子2）激活剂发挥作用。总之，本研究证明了PD149163的神经保护作用，可能通过调节Nrf2通路实现。
